method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Syncope** = brief, sudden loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery. About 15% of children have an episode by the end of adolescence.
claims.source_text: Syncope is a brief and sudden loss of consciousness associated with loss of postural tone with spontaneous recovery … Paediatric syncope is common, with about 15% of children experiencing an episode before the end of adolescence
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **An arrhythmia should be considered in every child with syncope**, even though most paediatric syncope is vasovagal. A thorough history is the best guide to cause and investigation.
claims.source_text: An arrhythmia should be considered in all children with syncope Most paediatric syncope is vasovagal A thorough history is the best strategy to determine the cause of syncope and guide further investigation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflex (vasovagal) syncope** has a clear precipitant — tiredness, hunger, heat, dehydration, emotion.
claims.source_text: Reflex syncope Eg vasovagal syncope Clear precipitating event, eg tiredness, hunger, heat, dehydration, emotion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Orthostatic hypotension:** within 2–3 minutes of standing, systolic falls over 20 mmHg or diastolic over 10 mmHg. Causes include hypovolaemia, anaemia, electrolyte disturbance, menorrhagia, medications.
claims.source_text: Orthostatic hypotension Within 2-3 minutes of assuming an upright position: decrease in systolic blood pressure >20 mmHg or decrease in diastolic blood pressure of >10 mmHg Causes include hypovolaemia, anaemia, electrolyte abnormalities, menorrhagia, medications
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **POTS:** daily chronic orthostatic intolerance **and**, within 5–10 minutes of standing, a heart-rate rise over 40 bpm, or over 30 bpm without postural hypotension.
claims.source_text: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) Daily symptoms of chronic orthostatic intolerance and Within 5-10 minutes of assuming an upright position: HR increase >40 bpm or HR increase >30 bpm without postural hypotension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac causes:** brady/tachyarrhythmia, long QT, Brugada, CPVT, conduction disease such as WPW, and structural disease (congenital heart disease, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis).
claims.source_text: Cardiac Brady/tachyarrhythmia Long QT syndrome Brugada syndrome Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia Conduction disease eg Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome Structural abnormalities eg congenital heart disease, cardiomyopathies, myocarditis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mimics:** seizure, migraine, hypoglycaemia, toxins (carbon monoxide, clonidine), functional disorder, narcolepsy.
claims.source_text: Differential diagnoses Seizure Migraine Hypoglycaemia Toxin exposure eg carbon monoxide, clonidine Functional disorder Narcolepsy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unconsciousness:** usually seconds in autonomic and cardiogenic syncope; **more than a few seconds, up to minutes, in seizures.**
claims.source_text: Feature Autonomic syncope Cardiogenic syncope Seizures … Period of unconsciousness Usually seconds Usually seconds Usually more than a few seconds, up to minutes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incontinence** is absent in autonomic and cardiogenic syncope and may be present in seizures; **confusion on waking** is absent in both syncope types and **marked for 20–30 minutes after a seizure.**
claims.source_text: Feature Autonomic syncope Cardiogenic syncope Seizures … Incontinence Absent Absent May be present Confusion on waking Absent Absent Marked for 20-30 mins
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tonic-clonic movements** are occasional and brief in either syncope type, particularly with prolonged unconsciousness (syncopal seizure); **frequent in seizures.**
claims.source_text: Feature Autonomic syncope Cardiogenic syncope Seizures … Tonic-clonic movements, presence and timing Occasionally and brief particularly if unconsciousness is prolonged (syncopal seizure) Occasionally and brief particularly if unconsciousness is prolonged (syncopal seizure) Frequently present
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure orthostatic heart rate and BP**, and do a complete cardiac and neurological examination.
claims.source_text: Orthostatic heart rate and blood pressure measurements Complete cardiac and neurological examination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ECG in every child at least once** — may be skipped only if done before with no new concern.
claims.source_text: ECG should be obtained in all children at least once. May not be required if done previously and there is no additional concern
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BGL** if seen soon after the event, **FBE** if anaemia is suspected, and consider a pregnancy test.
claims.source_text: BGL can be useful if the child is seen shortly after the event FBE (if anaemia is suspected) Consider pregnancy testing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Frequent or problematic vasovagal or orthostatic syncope:** avoid triggers, **increase fluid and salt intake**, and recognise prodromal symptoms early.
claims.source_text: Children with frequent and/or problematic vasovagal or orthostatic syncope Avoid usual triggers Increase fluid and salt intake Early recognition of prodromal symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected cardiac syncope on history, examination or ECG: refer urgently to a paediatrician or cardiologist.**
claims.source_text: Suspicion of cardiac syncope on history, examination or ECG. Urgently refer to a paediatrician or cardiologist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer** recurrent vasovagal/orthostatic syncope unresponsive to non-drug measures (paediatrician or cardiologist), and seizure-like presentations (paediatrician or neurologist).
claims.source_text: Children with recurrent vasovagal or orthostatic syncope that do not respond to non-pharmacological treatment. Refer to paediatrician or cardiologist Children with presentations suspicious for seizures. Refer to paediatrician or neurologist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** if persistently symptomatic, or with clustering of syncope with cardiac features.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Children are persistently symptomatic on assessment Children with clustering of syncope with cardiac features
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** once the most likely cause is identified and follow-up is arranged.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when The most likely cause of syncope has been identified and follow up has been arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23
